'''''Salvia wagneriana''''' is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] found in [[Nicaragua]], [[Costa Rica]], [[Guatemala]], [[El Salvador]], and the Mexican state of [[Chiapas]], growing at {{convert|4000|to|6500|ft|m}} elevation in warm, moist areas. 

==Description==
''Salvia wagneriana'' grows up to {{convert|9|ft|m}} tall and {{convert|4|ft|m}} wide, with yellow-green leaves that sometimes have purple veins. The underside of the leaf has raised veins. The flowers range in color from bright red to rose to pinkish cream, with highly colored [[bract]]s and [[Calyx (botany)|calyces]] that are different colors than the flower. The showy flowers are {{convert|1|to|3|in|cm}} long.<ref name="Clebsch"/>

==Cultivation==
It is very popular among gardeners near its native habitat, and one of the few native plants taken from the wild by local gardeners. It is described sometimes as a [[herb]] and sometimes as a [[shrub]] by various botanists.<ref name="Clebsch">{{cite book|last1=Clebsch|first1=Betsy|last2=Barner|first2=Carol D.|title=The New Book of Salvias|publisher=Timber Press|date=2003|page=305|isbn=978-0-88192-560-9|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NM0iwB8GrQYC&pg=PA305}}</ref>
